how: Moves read off the chess.com move list in the frames; every move graded by Stockfish 10 (chess-reader.js scoreGame via chess-grade.mjs) at depth 16 and again at depth 20, with Stockfish's line taken at depth 18 for each graded position. The engine's own best move shows losses up to about 100 cp at these depths (1.e4: 101 at depth 16, 59 at depth 20; 8.d4: 62 / 25), so only losses of 250+ (blunders) are firm and 100-250 (mistakes) are soft. White moves graded 100+ at both depths: 6.Ne2 (151 / 121), 10.Qb5+ (168 / 116), 11.Qe5+ (138 / 113), 12.Bd2 (104 / 137), 15.Bc3 (169 / 211), 26.Rf1 (147 / 160); listed below are the blunders, 15.Bc3 (over 200 at depth 20), 26.Rf1, and 21.Rhf1 (119 / 88, kept as a borderline case).
habit: Moving quickly without checking what the opponent can capture or fork after the move: 15.Bc3 (one to two seconds' thought) onto the square ...Nd5 forks with the e3 queen; 16.Qd3 onto the c4-e2 line, open to ...Bc4; 18.Nf4 about a second after the queen trade, onto the d6 bishop's diagonal to the king; and at move 22, with two black bishops hanging, taking the wrong one first.
